result:
The spec's 11 rulings reduce to 7 outcomes. R1 and R3 merge into one. R5 and R11 describe how the system is built and configured, so I've listed them as choices, not outcomes. The list below is unranked.

## Outcomes

| # | Outcome (what you get) | From | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A filing-index catalog in Parquet, with provenance, for a quarter range you choose | R1, R3 | About 30–60 MB per recent quarter, low single-digit GB back to 1993. Basis: about 350k rows × about 90 bytes per `master.idx` line, with early quarters much smaller. Not verified. Requests are trivial: a few hundred at 3/s. |
| O2 | Daily indexes added to the catalog, catching up after missed runs and across quarter boundaries | R2 | About 0.5–1 MB per daily file and about 250 files a year (quarterly size ÷ about 63 business days). A year's catch-up takes minutes of requests. |
| O3 | Later changes to past quarters (additions, field changes, withdrawals) recorded, with closed-quarter withdrawals held until you approve them by hash | R7, R10 | **Material.** §4.2 refreshes every supported quarter weekly, which re-downloads the whole archive, several GB, every week. Conditional requests might cut that; only a real run can tell. |
| O4 | Stored source files reprocessed after a parser change, with no new SEC downloads | R6 | Storage of the raw bytes ≈ O1's volume. Compute is negligible at this size. |
| O5 | Readers see only complete, versioned quarter datasets through one active pointer | R9 | Negligible beyond O1. |
| O6 | All SEC traffic from backfill, daily and reconciliation under one shared request budget, even when the runs overlap | R8 | Negligible compute. It caps how fast O1–O3 can run. |
| O7 | The whole thing running on Azure: ADF schedules, Container Apps jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, alerts and runbooks | R4 | Azure spend is unknown until the first real deployment measures it. It also takes your time to provision identities and roles. |

## Proposed tracks

- **Track A: the catalog (O1–O5).** Known progression. All five run on real SEC data from a laptop.
- **Track B: Azure operation (O6, O7).** Known progression, following spec §7's phases.

I split them because they serve different uses. A answers "do I have a correct, replayable filing index?", while B answers "does it run unattended in the cloud?". If they stay joined, the first real catalog waits on ADF, managed identity and Container Apps.

O6 sits in B because a single local collector already holds the whole budget. The shared lease only matters when collectors overlap. The 3 req/s ceiling and the User-Agent apply from A's first request regardless.

One alternative: O3 could be a **research** track. Whether the hash-bound withdrawal gate earns its complexity depends on how often closed quarters actually change, and nobody has measured that.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14, uv workspace (`.python-version`, root `pyproject.toml`).
- Platform: Azure per the ADR. The ADR and spec are both still **Proposed**, so tell me whether this counts as decided.
- Shared downloader, parser and publisher across all modes (R5).
- The §4.8 numbers are starting defaults (R11).
- Layout: there are four scaffold packages, but §4.9 names only `sec-edgar-ingest`. Which package holds what is left to each stage's design.

## Proposed name

`sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec`, which gives `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md`. That's the spec's stem, used whole.

**Optional probe:** to firm up O1–O3's cost notes, I can fetch one real quarterly and one daily `master.idx` and record their sizes. It only runs if you say yes. It needs the User-Agent identity you want the SEC to see (`sec.user_agent`, organization plus contact email).

**Your call, in one reply:**
- Rank the outcomes within each track and rank the tracks against each other.
- Confirm or change the tracks, their kinds (including O3 as research or not) and the name.
